'''Ngô Bảo Châu''' ({{IPA|vi|ŋo ɓa᷉ːw cəw|lang}}, born 28 June 1972)<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.math.uchicago.edu/~ngo/nbc-homepage.html|title=Homepage at University of Chicago|author=University of Chicago|publisher=University of Chicago|date=15 March 2011|access-date=20 August 2011}}</ref> is a Vietnamese-French [[mathematician]] at the [[University of Hong Kong]], best known for proving the [[Fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|fundamental lemma for automorphic forms]] (proposed by [[Robert Langlands]] and [[Diana Shelstad]]). He is the first Vietnamese national to have received the [[Fields Medal]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bellos |first=Alex |date=19 August 2010 |title=Mathematics 'Nobel' rewards boundary-busting work |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/dn19337-mathematics-nobel-rewards-boundary-busting-work/ |access-date=21 November 2024 |website=[[New Scientist]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=April 2011 |title=Asia Pacific Mathematics Newsletter April 2011 |url=https://www.austms.org.au/Publ/APMN/APMN_V1_N2_Electronic.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170303193450/http://www.austms.org.au/Publ/APMN/APMN_V1_N2_Electronic.pdf |archive-date=3 March 2017 |access-date=21 November 2024 |publisher=The Australian Mathematical Society}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://tuoitre.com.vn/Tianyon/Index.aspx?ArticleID=108794&ChannelID=13|title=Hiện tượng Ngô Bảo Châu|newspaper=Tuổi trẻ Online|author=Hàm Châu|date=18 November 2005|access-date=9 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100301034010/http://tuoitre.com.vn/Tianyon/Index.aspx?ArticleID=108794&ChannelID=13|archive-date=1 March 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://tuoitre.com.vn/Tianyon/Index.aspx?ArticleID=116027&ChannelID=17|title=10 sự kiện khoa học&nbsp;— công nghệ nổi bật năm 2005|newspaper=Tuổi trẻ Online|author=K.Hưng|date=29 December 2005|access-date=19 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100217020313/http://tuoitre.com.vn/Tianyon/Index.aspx?ArticleID=116027&ChannelID=17|archive-date=17 February 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hạ Anh |last2=Hương Giang |date=19 August 2010 |title=GS Griffiths: 'Trong giới Toán học, anh Châu vẫn là người Việt' |url=https://vnn.vietnamnet.vn/giaoduc/201008/GS-Griffiths-Trong-gioi-Toan-hoc-anh-Chau-van-la-nguoi-Viet-930131/ |access-date=21 November 2024 |website=Vietnamnet}}</ref>

==Early life==
Ngô Bảo Châu was born in 1972, the son of an intellectual family in [[Hanoi]], [[North Vietnam]]. His father, professor {{Interlanguage link|Ngô Huy Cẩn|vi}}, is full professor of physics at the Vietnam National Institute of Mechanics. His mother, Trần Lưu Vân Hiền, is a physician and associate professor at an herbal medicine hospital in Hanoi.

The beginning of Châu's schooling was at an experimental elementary school that had been founded by the revolutionary pedagogue Hồ Ngọc Đại, but when his father returned from the Soviet Union with his doctoral degree, he decided that Châu would learn more in traditional schools and enrolled him in the "chuyên toán" (special classes for gifted students in mathematics) at the Trưng Vương Middle School.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Koblitz |first=Neal |date=1 March 2011 |title=Interview with Professor Ngô Ba̓o Châu |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00283-010-9184-1 |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |language=en |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=46–50 |doi=10.1007/s00283-010-9184-1 |issn=1866-7414|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
At age 15, Châu entered the special mathematics class at the [[High School for Gifted Students, Hanoi University of Science]] (Khối chuyên Tổng Hợp&nbsp;– Đại học Khoa Học Tự Nhiên Hà Nội<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hus.edu.vn/?portal=home&obj=intro_daotao&id=745|title=Đại học Khoa Học Tự Nhiên Hà Nội|publisher=HUS-VNU official website|access-date=19 August 2010}}</ref>), formerly known as the A0-class. In grades 11 and 12, Châu participated in the 29th and 30th [[International Mathematical Olympiad]]s (IMO) and became the first Vietnamese student to win two IMO gold medals,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=1573|title=Ngô Bảo Châu|publisher=IMO's official website|access-date=12 October 2009}}</ref> of which the first one was won with a perfect score (42/42).<ref name=lecourrier>{{cite news|url=http://lecourrier.vnagency.com.vn/PrintView.asp?id=49751|language=fr|title=Ngô Bao Châu, sommité mondiale des maths|author=Ham Chau|newspaper=Le Courrier du Vietnam|date=15 February 2009}}</ref>

After high school, Châu expected to study in [[Budapest]], but in the aftermath of the fall of [[Communism]] in [[Eastern Europe]], the new [[Hungary|Hungarian]] government halted scholarships to students from Vietnam.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://dantri.com.vn/c20/s20-416055/ngo-bao-chau-bom-tan-va-trong-dong-trong-toan-hoc.htm|language=vi|title=Ngô Bảo Châu, "bom tấn" và "trống đồng" trong toán học|author=Hàm Châu|publisher=Dân Trí|date=17 August 2010}}</ref> After visiting Châu's father, Paul Germain, secretary of the [[French Academy of Sciences]], arranged for Châu to study in France. He was offered a scholarship by the French government for undergraduate study at the [[Paris VI University]], then in 1992, he entered the [[École Normale Supérieure]]. He obtained a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1997 from the [[Universite Paris-Sud]] under the supervision of [[Gérard Laumon]].  He became a member of [[CNRS]] at [[Sorbonne Paris North University|Sorbonne Paris North University]] from 1998 to 2005, and defended his [[habilitation]] degree there in 2003. He holds both Vietnamese and French citizenship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://smai.emath.fr/IMG/pdf_ICM-L1v3l.pdf|title=Le congrès international des mathématiciens|publisher=Société Mathématique de France|access-date=7 July 2010}}</ref>

==Career==
Châu became a professor at [[Paris-Sud 11 University]] in 2005. In 2005, at age 33, Châu received the title of professor in Vietnam, becoming the country's youngest-ever professor.<ref name=lecourrier/>  Since 2007, Châu has worked at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]], [[Princeton, New Jersey]], as well as the Hanoi Institute of Mathematics.<ref name=time/> He joined the mathematics faculty at the [[University of Chicago]] on 1 September 2010. In addition, since 2011 he has been Scientific Director of the newly founded Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (VIASM).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://viasm.edu.vn/en/about-the-institute/history-html|title=History|publisher=Vietnam Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics|access-date=15 March 2019}}</ref> In 2016 Châu was Co-General Chair of [[Asiacrypt]] the first time that the Asian cryptography conference was held in Vietnam.<ref>{{cite web|title=Asiacrypt 2016 Organizing Committee|url=https://www.iacr.org/conferences/asiacrypt2016/www.asiacrypt2016.org/indexe735.html?page_id=85|access-date=11 April 2018}}</ref> Starting 1 July 2023, Châu has been serving as the new Chair of the Department of Mathematics at the University of Chicago.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A delicate balance {{!}} News {{!}} Physical Sciences Division {{!}} The University of Chicago |url=https://physicalsciences.uchicago.edu/news/article/a-delicate-balance/ |access-date=30 January 2024 |website=physicalsciences.uchicago.edu}}</ref>

On 5 February, the [[University of Hong Kong]] announced that Châu is to join the Department of Mathematics from June 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 February 2026 |title=Fields Medalist Professor Ngô Bảo Châu Joins HKU as Chair Professor |url=https://www.hku.hk/press/press-releases/detail/28928.html |access-date=7 February 2026 |website=www.hku.hk |language=en}}</ref>

==Work==
Châu first came to prominence by proving, in joint work with [[Gérard Laumon]], the [[Fundamental lemma (Langlands program)|fundamental lemma]] for [[unitary group]]s. Their general strategy was to understand the local [[orbital integral]]s appearing in the fundamental lemma in terms of [[Affine bundle|affine Springer fiber]]s arising in the [[Hitchin fibration]]. This allowed them to employ the tools of geometric [[representation theory]], namely the theory of [[perverse sheaves]], to study what was initially a [[combinatorics|combinatorial]] problem of a [[number theory|number-theoretic]] nature. Chau eventually succeeded in formulating the proof for the fundamental lemma for [[Lie algebra]]s in 2008.<ref name=lecourrier/> Together with earlier results from [[Jean-Loup Waldspurger]], who had shown that the full fundamental lemma results from this then missing result, this completed the proof of the fundamental lemma in all cases. As a result, Châu was awarded a [[Fields Medal]] in 2010.

Ngô Bảo Châu was the co-author of the Vietnamese children's book ''Ai and Ky in the land of the invisible numbers''.

==Awards==
In 2004, Châu and Laumon were awarded the [[Clay Research Award]] for their achievement in solving the fundamental lemma for the case of [[unitary group]]s.<ref name=lecourrier/> Châu's proof of the general case was selected by [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] as one of the Top Ten Scientific Discoveries of 2009.<ref name=time>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,1945379_1944416_1944435,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213010530/http://www.time.com/time/specials/packages/article/0,28804,1945379_1944416_1944435,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=13 December 2009|magazine=Time magazine|title=Top 10 Scientific Discoveries of 2009|date=8 December 2009}}</ref> In 2010, he received the [[Fields Medal]]. By decree on 22 April 2011, he was awarded a [[Knight]] of France's [[Legion of Honour]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ordre National De La Legion D'honneur|trans-title=National Order of the Legion of Honour|date=22 April 2011|url=http://legiondhonneur.fr/shared/fr/promo/lh/jo110422lhpromotionpaque.html|access-date=20 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120215224638/http://legiondhonneur.fr/shared/fr/promo/lh/jo110422lhpromotionpaque.html|archive-date=15 February 2012}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 10 November 2012.</ref> In 2021, he became an honorary member of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=LMS Honorary Members 2021|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/node/1712|access-date=6 July 2021|website=London Mathematical Society|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|title=Ngô Bao Châu élu membre honoraire de la London Mathematical Society|url=https://www.lecourrier.vn/ngo-bao-chau-elu-membre-honoraire-de-la-london-mathematical-society/924128.html|access-date=6 July 2021|website=Le Courrier du Vietnam|language=fr}}</ref>
